summary: This is a Snowflake documentation page for the IS_<object_type> family of Boolean predicate functions, which determine the data type of a VARIANT value. All functions are unary, take one VARIANT argument, and return FALSE for SQL NULL or VARIANT null input. The examples use a vartab table with rows of null, NULL, boolean, integer, decimal, double, varchar, array and object values to show which predicates match which types.
one_line: Reference for the IS_<object_type> Boolean predicate functions that test the data type of VARIANT values, with examples.
key_facts: The IS_ _ <object_type> family of functions serves as Boolean predicates that determine the data type of a value stored in a VARIANT column.
All IS_ functions are unary, taking a VARIANT expression as the only argument.
All IS_ functions return FALSE if the input is SQL NULL or the VARIANT expression contains null.
The examples use a table named vartab, created in the PARSE_JSON documentation, with columns n and v.
Row 1 of vartab has the VARIANT value null, whose typeof is NULL_VALUE.
Row 2 of vartab is SQL NULL, whose typeof is NULL.
Row 3 of vartab is true, whose typeof is BOOLEAN.
Row 4 of vartab is -17, whose typeof is INTEGER.
Row 5 of vartab is 123.12, whose typeof is DECIMAL.
Row 6 of vartab is 1.912000000000000e+02, whose typeof is DOUBLE.
Row 7 of vartab is the string "Om ara pa ca na dhih", whose typeof is VARCHAR.
Row 8 of vartab is an array containing -1, 12, 289, 2188, false and undefined, whose typeof is ARRAY.
Row 9 of vartab is an object with keys x ("abc"), y (false) and z (10), whose typeof is OBJECT.
Using is_char(v) on vartab returns a count of 1, matching only the string row.
is_integer(v) matches only the -17 row, while is_decimal(v) matches both -17 and 123.12, and is_double(v) matches -17, 123.12 and 1.912e+02.
